description: The default configuration file that Spring Boot loads from the classpath and the working directory at startup.
An annotation that binds a group of properties with a common prefix to a typed class, such as a record.
The rule that lets one property be written in kebab case, camel case or as an upper-case environment variable.
A named environment, such as dev or prod, that activates extra configuration documents and beans.
A setting that activates several profiles together when one named profile is active.
The ranking in which config files, environment variables, system properties and command-line arguments override each other.
A folder of files, often mounted secrets, whose file names become property names and whose contents become values.
